notes: Upshift's built-in catalog. Upshift will later download a newer version of this file from its GitHub repo, so new forks and GPU support can be added without releasing a new version. The userAgent values below are fallbacks; the app sends Upshift/<its version>.

components.name: OptiScaler
components.description: The official OptiScaler. Adds the Insert-key menu for switching between DLSS, FSR and XeSS and turning on frame generation.
components.notes: Stable = pinnedVersion. When a release has several matching files (the old nightly has five), the one with the highest version in its name is used.

components.name: OptiScaler DLSSNR
components.description: OptiScaler fork that adds NVIDIA DLSS 5 Neural Rendering. Needs the user's own nvngx_dlssnr.dll.

components.name: AMD-NR
components.description: OptiScaler fork that runs DLSS 5 Neural Rendering on AMD RX 7000 and RX 9000 cards. Includes the lmxxf runtime.

components.name: AMD-NR runtime (danielblnc)
components.description: Extra runtime that AMD-NR needs on RX 7000 cards (optional on RX 9000). Must match the AMD-NR version.
components.notes: Runtime file names vary (Runtime.zip, v0.3.1-Runtime.zip) and some releases carry two (v0.4.0- and v0.4.1-Runtime.zip); the highest version is used.

components.name: dlssg-to-fsr3
components.description: Nukem9's mod that lets a game's DLSS Frame Generation option run FSR 3 frame generation. Bundled with OptiScaler 0.9 and newer.
components.notes: Its recent GitHub releases have no files attached (only 0.3 and 0.21 from 2023 do). OptiScaler 0.9+ bundles it; the version comes from OptiScaler's release notes ("Nukems dlssg_to_fsr3 0.130").

components.name: fakenvapi
components.description: Lets non-NVIDIA cards use a game's Reflex option through Anti-Lag 2, LatencyFlex or XeLL. Bundled with OptiScaler 0.9 and newer.

components.name: NVIDIA DLSS
components.description: NVIDIA's own DLSS files, for updating the DLSS a game shipped with.
components.notes: The DLLs are read from the repository at the release tag (release files are only demos) and checked against the git blob hash GitHub reports. lib/Windows_x86_64/rel has nvngx_dlss.dll (SR), nvngx_dlssd.dll (RR) and nvngx_dlssg.dll (FG); dev/ has watermarked builds, never used.

components.name: AMD FidelityFX (FSR)
components.description: AMD's FidelityFX SDK, for updating FSR 3.1+ files a game shipped with.
components.notes: Game files come straight from the repo (upscalerFiles): the signed DLLs are in PrebuiltSignedDLL/ (v1.x) and Kits/FidelityFX/signedbin/ (v2.x), so the 130-470 MB zips aren't needed. v2.3.0 only ships FidelityFX-Samples-…-prebuilt.zip, v2.0.0 ships FidelityFX-SDK-….zip and v2.1.x ship no files.

components.name: Intel XeSS
components.description: Intel's XeSS SDK, for updating XeSS files a game shipped with.
components.notes: The SDK version isn't the DLLs' version: SDK 3.0.2 has libxess.dll 2.0.2.68, libxess_fg.dll 1.3.1.78 and libxell.dll 1.3.2.10. SDK 1.3.1's zip is XeSS_SDK-1.3.1.zip with the files under XeSS_SDK-1.3.1/bin/.

upscalerFiles.notes: Newer copies of upscaler DLLs that games ship. A game's file is only replaced by one with the same name, never added, and only when its version is in [minVersion, belowVersion) and older than 'version'. Checked 2026-09-28: DLSS 2.0+ SR and 3.5+ RR use the same NGX interface (DLSS 1.x doesn't). FSR 3.1's amd_fidelityfx_dx12/vk.dll (1.0.x) go to 3.1.4, the last single-DLL release; SDK 2.x's loader needs the separate upscaler DLL next to it, which would mean adding files. XeSS stays within its major version (Intel: a major version 'indicates a new API, and potentially a break'), and XeSS 1.x only from 1.3 (1.3 changed the resolution scaling). DLSS Frame Generation isn't offered: it's paired with the game's Streamline version. All sources are 64-bit.

neuralBackends.name: AMD-NR
neuralBackends.summary: Uses the AMD-NR fork of OptiScaler. No NVIDIA file needed. Press Home in-game to turn it on and off.

neuralBackends.name: OptiScaler DLSSNR
neuralBackends.summary: Uses the NVIDIA DLSS 5 fork of OptiScaler with your own DLSS 5 file (nvngx_dlssnr.dll).

neuralBackends.name: OptiScaler DLSSNR
neuralBackends.summary: NVIDIA's official DLSS 5 file only runs on RTX 50 cards for now. It works on this card with a modified file you supply, which can't be verified as safe. RTX 40 support is expected from NVIDIA this fall.

pcGamingWiki.userAgent: Upshift/1.0 (Upshift for Windows; reads engine and upscaler info)

recommendations.notes: Suggestions only, never requirements. First rule whose vendor and generation match wins. {gpu} is the card's name. 'upscaler' is used when the game has it; 'upscalerViaOptiScaler' when it only has other upscalers.

rules.reason: NVIDIA's own upscaler runs on your card's Tensor cores and usually looks best.
rules.frameGenReason: RTX 40 and 50 cards can run NVIDIA's frame generation.

rules.reason: NVIDIA's own upscaler runs on your card's Tensor cores and usually looks best.
rules.frameGenReason: DLSS frame generation needs an RTX 40 or 50, so FSR frame generation is the one that runs here.

rules.reason: Without Tensor cores DLSS isn't available; XeSS usually looks better than FSR 3 on these cards.
rules.frameGenReason: FSR frame generation works on any recent card.

rules.reason: FSR 4 is AMD's machine-learning upscaler and is made for RX 9000 cards.
rules.frameGenReason: AMD's frame generation, with the FSR 4 version on RX 9000 cards.

rules.reason: FSR 4 (INT8) is officially supported on RX 7000 desktop cards since OptiScaler 0.9.4.
XeSS or FSR 3.1 run well here. FSR 4 (INT8) is an optional extra you can try.
Intel's own upscaler uses your card's XMX units and usually looks best.

fallback.reason: The game's own engine upscaler is the safest choice when no DLSS, FSR or XeSS is available.

dlssPresets.name: DLSS 4.5 – Preset M
dlssPresets.note: Sharper, a bit slower. NVIDIA's default for Performance.

dlssPresets.name: DLSS 4.5 – Preset L (Ultra Performance)
dlssPresets.note: Sharpest and most stable, but slower. NVIDIA's default for Ultra Performance.

dlssPresets.name: DLSS 4 – Preset K
dlssPresets.note: Balanced quality and speed. NVIDIA's default for DLAA, Quality and Balanced.

dlssPresets.name: DLSS 4 – Preset J
dlssPresets.note: Like K with slightly less ghosting but more flicker.

fsr4.notes: FSR 4 is official on these generations, so the INT8 options are hidden there.

dlssModel.title: Which DLSS model should I pick?

rows.name: K (DLSS 4)
rows.text: Sharp and clean, and the lightest of the new models.

rows.name: J (DLSS 4)
rows.text: Like K, with slightly less ghosting but more flicker.

rows.name: M (DLSS 4.5)
rows.text: Noticeably sharper and more stable than K, and costs a bit more.

rows.name: L (DLSS 4.5)
rows.text: The sharpest and most stable, and the most expensive.

rows.name: Game default
rows.text: Let the game decide.

rows.name: NVIDIA recommended
rows.text: M for Performance, L for Ultra Performance, K for everything else.

cardNotes.text: M and L run at full speed on your card.
M and L cost more on your card; K is often the better choice.

rows.text: OptiScaler picks its own default for this game; choose one of the others to decide yourself.
NVIDIA's upscaler, and the best-looking choice on an RTX card.
Intel's upscaler: runs on your card in a generic mode that looks better than FSR 3.1 but costs a little more.

forCard.Intel: Intel's upscaler, running on your Arc card's own AI cores: the best choice on your card.

rows.text: AMD's AI upscaler in its INT8 version: clearly better than FSR 3.1, but it costs more on your card.

forCard.RDNA 4: AMD's newest, AI-based upscaler, made for your card: the best choice on it.

rows.text: AMD's upscaler that runs on any card: fast, but softer and with more shimmer than the AI upscalers.
An older FSR, only worth trying if FSR 3.1 misbehaves in this game.

cardNotes.text: On your card, DLSS is almost always the best choice.
On your card, FSR 4 is the best choice.
On your card, XeSS or FSR 4 (INT8) usually look better than FSR 3.1; FSR 3.1 is the fastest.
On your card, XeSS is the best choice.
Your card can't run DLSS; XeSS usually looks better than FSR 3.1, and FSR 3.1 is the fastest.

frameGen.title: Which frame generation should I pick?

rows.text: No generated frames: the lowest input lag.
The frame generation built into the game; turn it on in the game's own menu.
The game's DLSS frame generation option runs AMD's FSR frame generation instead, so it works without an RTX 40 card.
The game's DLSS frame generation is replaced by AMD's FSR frame generation.
The game's DLSS frame generation is replaced by Intel's XeSS frame generation (needs borderless windowed mode).
The game's own FSR frame generation, run through OptiScaler's newer FSR.
The game's FSR frame generation is replaced by Intel's XeSS frame generation (needs borderless windowed mode).
OptiScaler adds FSR frame generation to any game with an upscaler turned on; the HUD may smear without HUDfix.
OptiScaler adds XeSS frame generation to any game with an upscaler turned on (needs borderless windowed mode).

cardNotes.text: Your card has DLSS frame generation: if the game offers it, "Game's own" is usually best.

frameGen.footer: Frame generation makes motion smoother but adds input lag. It works best when the game already runs at 60 fps or more.
